newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Under-cover stripper was unfairly sacked by police.
newsitem.headline: Under-cover stripper was unfairly sacked by police.

text.p: A trainee policewoman sacked after senior officers discovered she had worked as a prostitute and stripper won an unfair dismissal case on Thursday and said she still hoped to have a good time in the force.
Kim Hollingsworth was sacked in 1995 as a trainee with the New South Wales state police for failing to reveal her past employment before becoming a police cadet.

While in the force, Hollingsworth had taken part in covert operations for a long-running police corruption inquiry and given evidence about police who had used her services as a call girl for Sydney's Black Garter brothel.
"I'm delighted with the decision...I do hope I get my job back in the future," Hollingsworth, 30, told reporters.
"That's been my dream since I was six years old and corrupt police will not be spoiling that for me," she said.
Hollingsworth said she had no ill-feeling toward the police and believed she could work successfully as a police officer despite her past troubles.

"Of course there are going to be some police officers who won't be happy," she said. "However, I'm sure when they work with me their attitude will change...I'm confident that I'll have a good time if I'm reinstated."

Industrial relations commissioner Peter Connor ruled the dismissal was "unfair" and "harsh" because Hollingsworth was under no obligation to provide information about her past work on her police application form.

"Also, the treatment of Ms Hollingsworth, a female trainee police officer, appears to me to be in stark contrast to the treatment of other serving male police officers involved in stripping or who had hired her as a stripper or prostitute," Connor told the hearing.
Connor directed both parties to begin conciliation talks.
